thread.title: News of an Amazon-Apple Team-Up Hit Best Buy Last Week. Now What?

title: News of an Amazon-Apple Team-Up Hit Best Buy Last Week. Now What?
text:
News of an Amazon-Apple Team-Up Hit Best Buy Last Week. Now What? By Nov. 12, 2018 11:50 a.m. ET Order Reprints Photograph by Mike Mozart Text size
It was a black Friday for Best Buy (ticker: BBY). Will the stock recover in time for Thanksgiving?
The tech retailer’s shares slid some 7% at the end of last week, amid reports of a partnership between Amazon.com (ticker: AMZN) and Apple (AAPL) seen as damaging for it and other sellers of Apple products. So far, they haven’t bounced back: Best Buy stock was about flat Monday morning at approximately $68.
Some analysts believe investors overreacted last week. The selloff, Loop Capital Markets’ Anthony Chukumba wrote Monday, “was overdone and presents a buying opportunity.”
Loop has an $88 price target on the shares, putting it among the bigger Best Buy bulls on Wall Street, according to FactSet. The average target on the stock is currently around $78.
Amazon and Apple didn’t immediately reply to requests for comment on Monday morning, though both companies confirmed the partnership via spokespeople to other outlets last week. Best Buy also didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment. Newsletter Sign-up
In reports, the deal was characterized as having Apple sell many products directly to consumers via Amazon, while requiring third-party sellers to apply to become authorized resellers.
In that context, it’s perhaps easy to see why Best Buy investors might be concerned about the expansion of another retailer’s role in selling a key company’s products. In a Manhattan Best Buy store on Monday morning, a large chunk of floor and promotional space was dedicated to Apple’s phones, tablets, and other products.
Chukumba believes Best Buy can weather an Amazon-and-Apple-related storm.
“While Amazon is undoubtedly a formidable retailer, we remind investors that unlike Best Buy, the online behemoth is also a significant competitor to Apple. In addition, we believe the financial impact to Best Buy of this move is unlikely to be material.
Morgan Stanley ’s analysts, however, believe Friday’s drop was “appropriate,” citing concerns that wider availability of Apple products on Amazon could give shoppers, many who may have long used Best Buy as their main Apple source, less reason to do so. Recommended Reading
